answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, like a pearl that only forms after a real deposit is left inside the shell. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but creating thousands means locking thousands of stakes, so the attack cost grows linearly while honest agents recover their bond. A bridge of independent attestors verifies the stake and the agent work history before it joins the reef of trusted participants, and misbehavior slashes the bond, making mass fakery unprofitable.
